source_review.notes: Reviewed PostgreSQL 18 INSERT/ON CONFLICT, UPDATE, DELETE, and MERGE documentation; SQLite UPSERT and ON CONFLICT documentation; and MySQL 8.4 ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE and REPLACE documentation. All eight official destinations returned HTTP 200. Arbiter, deterministic-source, RETURNING, affected-row, conflict-order, replacement, and concurrency claims are scoped by dialect and version.

evidence: Checked guarded transition W, stored state, identity, version, value, token, digest, and idempotence notation.
Checked that proposed, existing, affected, returned, committed, audited, and externally published states remain distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Atomic database transition and external side effects are separated through the transactional outbox boundary.

evidence: Recomputed event outcomes as update, replay, stale, insert, version conflict, insert, replay.
Recomputed final t1/a as version 3 value 15, preserved t1/b, inserted t1/c, and independently inserted t2/a.
Recomputed outcome counts as two inserts, two replays, one stale, one update, and one version conflict.
Recomputed audit rows only for the one update and two inserts with exact old/new pairs.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All fixture versions and values are bounded exact integers.

evidence: Re-derived insert from absent identity, advance from greater version, stale from lower version, and conflict from equal version with divergent payload.
Re-derived payload-bound replay from identical token and request tuple.
Verified applying an identical committed request again leaves domain state unchanged.
Re-derived lost-update prevention from atomic expected-version guard and exactly-one affected outcome.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Upsert alone is not claimed to make non-idempotent transitions retry-safe.

evidence: Reviewed absent/present target, insert, update, no-op, replay, token conflict, stale, equal-version conflict, tombstone, null, and constraint failure.
Reviewed duplicate source keys, multiple unique arbiters, defaults, generated values, triggers, cascades, partitions, policies, and source snapshots.
Reviewed same-key concurrency, lost update, relative counters, deadlock, serialization retry, timeout before/after commit, and connection loss.
Reviewed bulk batching, lock order, log volume, replication lag, audit/outbox atomicity, cancellation, rollback/repair, and upgrades.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Cross-row invariants may require constraints, serializable isolation, or explicit locking beyond a row version.

evidence: Validated tenant plus entity forms identity, so t1/a and t2/a do not conflict.
Validated versions never regress and divergent equal-version input does not change state.
Validated identical tokens do not create duplicate audit entries or state changes.
The verifier matched exact four-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status.
invariant_checking.notes: The model is sequential and does not certify locks, transactions, crashes, or durable token storage.

evidence: Reviewed every event against token history, identity presence, and version ordering in sequence.
Reviewed each mutation's exact old and new values and every nonmutation reason.
Reviewed final rows by folding the seven events over the two-row initial state.
Reviewed optimistic-control and idempotency arguments against their uniqueness and atomicity assumptions.
proof_review.notes: No proof of universal MERGE/upsert equivalence, external exactly-once delivery, or physical resource bounds is claimed.

evidence: Separated preflight selection from atomic guard, duplicate key from valid replay, upsert from idempotency, and statement result from commit outcome.
Separated affected-row count from business action, soft delete from physical delete, and database atomicity from external publication.
Separated PostgreSQL ON CONFLICT, MERGE, SQLite UPSERT, MySQL duplicate-key update, and MySQL REPLACE semantics.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Atomic, deterministic, affected, committed, idempotent, replayed, safe, and portable claims require their named evidence.

evidence: The standard-library finite versioned-upsert model executed successfully through the repository verifier.
All eight final official reference destinations returned HTTP 200 on 2026-08-30.
Front matter, exact section order, corrected local links, ten examples, five exercises, five answers, and snippet expectations passed draft validation.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No live DML, unique-conflict race, MERGE, trigger, cascade, partition, row policy, lock, deadlock, isolation, timeout, crash, replication, or performance workload was executed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter consistently derives modification from target identity, guarded transitions, authoritative outcomes, constraints, concurrency, retries, and commit evidence.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed INSERT/SELECT, guarded UPDATE/DELETE, counters, arbiters, upsert variants, source duplicates, MERGE, REPLACE, idempotency, uncertain outcomes, RETURNING, triggers, policies, partitions, deadlocks, isolation, audit/outbox, bulk work, and upgrades.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet, seven-event state machine, ten distinct worked examples, and five derivation/design exercises progress from single-row guards to large CDC production evidence.

limitations: Internal authoring, official-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and model do not certify any live database DML, constraint/arbiter selection, affected-row count, RETURNING behavior, MERGE/upsert concurrency, trigger/cascade/partition/policy effect, lock/deadlock/isolation behavior, crash or uncertain commit, idempotency persistence, outbox delivery, replication, performance result, upgrade compatibility, or production fitness.
